test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-2) Official Paper (Held On: 13 June 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A 265 m long train is running at 61 km/h. In how much time (in seconds) will it cross another train of length 245 m running at 47 km/h in the opposite direction?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed (opposite direction) = 61 + 47 = 108 km/h

Convert to m/s = 108 × (5 ÷ 18) = 30 m/s

Total distance = 265 + 245 = 510 m

Time = Distance ÷ Speed = 510 ÷ 30 = 17 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 17 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a8821c2a1918e197e9829516ce89996b9c69d0728c3f22c3a65692859ca9ece.png] 

**Given:**

L₁ = 265 m, S₁ = 61 km/h

L₂ = 245 m, S₂ = 47 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Total Distance = L₁ + L₂

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = S₁ + S₂

Time = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 265 + 245 = 510 m

⇒ Relative Speed = 61 + 47 = 108 km/h

⇒ Speed in m/s = 108 × (5 ÷ 18) = 30 m/s

⇒ Time = 510 ÷ 30

⇒ Time = 17 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 17 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: S₁ − S₂ (where S₁ > S₂).

Speed Unit Conversion Tricks

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the value by (5 ÷ 18). Conversely, to convert m/s to km/h, multiply by (18 ÷ 5).

Crossing a Platform or Bridge

When a moving train crosses a stationary object with length (like a platform, bridge, or tunnel), the total distance covered is the length of the train plus the length of the object.
